clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old previously healthy male presented with a 9-month history of multisystem involvement including watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss (6 kg), nocturnal fever, oligoarthritis, and characteristic mucocutaneous lesions (multiple ulcers with necrotic crust on lower limbs, painful erythematous nodules, and penile ulcers). Initial workup revealed colonic ulcers on colonoscopy (sigmoid and proximal rectum) but negative tuberculin skin test and normal chest X-ray. Diagnostic confirmation was achieved through skin biopsy of a lower limb ulcer demonstrating epithelioid granulomatous inflammation with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis (E007), followed by microbiological confirmation via Ziehl-Neelsen staining showing intact acid-fast bacilli and positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (E008). Intestinal biopsies showed only mild inflammatory infiltrate without visible bacilli (E009), suggesting either sampling limitation or reactive changes. The combination of chronic systemic symptoms, characteristic cutaneous findings, histopathological demonstration of caseating granulomas, and definitive microbiological isolation established the diagnosis of cutaneous tuberculosis with possible concurrent intestinal involvement.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Caseating granulomatous inflammation with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis in skin ulcer biopsy
Positive acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining and positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis from skin lesion
Chronic multisystem presentation (9 months) with cutaneous ulcers, arthralgia, and colonic ulcers
Absence of immunosuppression and negative tuberculin skin test with normal chest X-ray, consistent with isolated cutaneous/intestinal TB without pulmonary involvement

Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with caseation rather than vasculitic changes
Normal chest X-ray and negative tuberculin skin test argue against active pulmonary TB
